documents.text: For behold, Nephi was baptizing, and prophesying, and preaching, crying repentance unto the people, showing signs and wonders, working miracles among the people, that they might know that the Christ must shortly come—
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 16:4** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records reactions to Samuel the Lamanite’s prophecy: believers seek Nephi, confess sins, and are baptized; unbelievers attack Samuel with stones and arrows but cannot hit him, then try to seize him, and he escapes to preach in his own country. It summarizes years 86–90 of the judges, noting continued pride, increasing wickedness, signs and angels appearing, and widespread skepticism, contention, and rumors stirred up by Satan.

He mentions prophets testifying, a forerunner who baptizes in Bethabara beyond Jordan, and the Messiah’s death and resurrection with manifestation to Gentiles by the Holy Ghost. It covers Israel scattered and gathered like an olive tree. Nephi desires revelation and warns of judgment and uncleanness.

The Lord commands Lehi to travel, and the Liahona appears to guide them; they depart, cross the river Laman, camp at Shazer, and hunt. Nephi breaks his steel bow; murmuring follows. Nephi makes a wooden bow; Lehi inquires of the Lord; writings on the ball change with faith. Nephi hunts successfully. Ishmael dies at Nahom; renewed murmuring leads to a plot to kill Lehi and Nephi until the Lord chastens them and they repent.

documents.text: And I, Mormon, being a descendant of Nephi, (and my father's name was Mormon) I remembered the things which Ammaron commanded me.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 1:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records Mormon beginning his record and recounting Ammaron’s charge to retrieve the plates at hill Shim in Antum. Mormon moves to Zarahemla; wars begin near Sidon between Nephites and Lamanites, followed by four years of peace. Wickedness spreads; disciples are taken away and miracles cease. Mormon is visited of the Lord but is forbidden to preach. Gadianton robbers, hidden treasures, sorceries, and witchcrafts increase.

query: What happened to the people of Ammonihah?

documents.text: But as to the people that were in the land of Ammonihah, they yet remained a hard-hearted and a stiffnecked people; and they repented not of their sins, ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil; for they were of the profession of Nehor, and did not believe in the repentance of their sins.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 15:15** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records Alma and Amulek fleeing Ammonihah to Sidom, where they meet believers who were cast out. Zeezrom lies sick with a fever and guilt, sends for them, affirms belief in Christ, and is healed through Alma’s prayer, then baptized and begins preaching. Alma establishes a church in Sidom and ordains priests and teachers as many are baptized. Ammonihah remains unrepentant. Amulek loses wealth and family support; Alma and Amulek return to Zarahemla.

documents.text: And thus ended the eleventh year of the judges, the Lamanites having been driven out of the land, and the people of Ammonihah were destroyed; yea, every living soul of the Ammonihahites was destroyed, and also their great city, which they said God could not destroy, because of its greatness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 16:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Lamanite armies destroying Ammonihah, taking captives, and Zoram with sons Lehi and Aha seeking Alma’s guidance. Alma prophesies the Lamanite route; the Nephite army meets them east of Sidon near Manti, rescues all captives, and drives the Lamanites away. Ammonihah becomes the Desolation of Nehors. After years of peace, Alma, Amulek, and others preach repentance, condemn sins, and teach Christ’s coming, death, resurrection, and appearance after resurrection.

documents.text: And now it came to pass, before the Nephites could raise a sufficient army to drive them out of the land, they had destroyed the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, and also some around the borders of Noah, and taken others captive into the wilderness.

And now so great was the scent thereof that the people did not go in to possess the land of Ammonihah for many years. And it was called Desolation of Nehors; for they were of the profession of Nehor, who were slain; and their lands remained desolate.

documents.text: Now Satan had gotten great hold upon the hearts of the people of the city of Ammonihah; therefore they would not hearken unto the words of Alma.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 8:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records Alma returning from Gideon to Zarahemla, then preaching and baptizing in Melek. He travels to Ammonihah, is rejected, reviled, and cast out. An angel commands Alma to return and warn of destruction unless the people repent. Alma meets Amulek, is fed, stays with him, then both are called to preach repentance, filled with the Holy Ghost, and given power amid imprisonment.

documents.text: Behold, I said that the city of Ammonihah had been rebuilt. I say unto you, yea, that it was in part rebuilt; and because the Lamanites had destroyed it once because of the iniquity of the people, they supposed that it would again become an easy prey for them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 49:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Lamanite armies approaching rebuilt Ammonihah and being thwarted by Moroni’s fortifications. The Lamanites retreat to attack the city of Noah, where Lehi commands and defenses include banks, ditches, and guarded entrances. Lamanite assaults fail; chief captains are slain and over a thousand die, while no Nephites are killed and about fifty are wounded. Amalickiah reacts with anger and oaths, while Nephites give thanks; the year ends with peace and church prosperity under Helaman, Shiblon, Corianton, and Ammon.

documents.text: For behold, the armies of the Lamanites had come in upon the wilderness side, into the borders of the land, even into the city of Ammonihah, and began to slay the people and destroy the city.

documents.text: And it came to pass that Alma and Amulek were commanded to depart out of that city; and they departed, and came out even into the land of Sidom; and behold, there they found all the people who had departed out of the land of Ammonihah, who had been cast out and stoned, because they believed in the words of Alma.

Alma establishes a church in Sidom and ordains priests and teachers as many are baptized. Ammonihah remains unrepentant. Amulek loses wealth and family support; Alma and Amulek return to Zarahemla.

documents.text: And they brought their wives and children together, and whosoever believed or had been taught to believe in the word of God they caused that they should be cast into the fire; and they also brought forth their records which contained the holy scriptures, and cast them into the fire also, that they might be burned and destroyed by fire.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 14:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 29 verses and records many in Ammonihah believing Alma and Amulek, while others bind them and accuse them before the chief judge. Zeezrom confesses guilt and is cast out. Believers, their wives and children, and scriptures are burned, and Alma and Amulek are imprisoned, beaten, mocked, and deprived. On the twelfth day Alma prays; they break their cords, an earthquake destroys the prison and kills their persecutors, and they escape as the people flee.

documents.text: And it came to pass after they had thus suffered for many days, (and it was on the twelfth day, in the tenth month, in the tenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi) that the chief judge over the land of Ammonihah and many of their teachers and their lawyers went in unto the prison where Alma and Amulek were bound with cords.

documents.text: And behold, I am sent to command thee that thou return to the city of Ammonihah, and preach again unto the people of the city; yea, preach unto them. Yea, say unto them, except they repent the Lord God will destroy them.

documents.text: And it came to pass that Alma and Amulek, Amulek having forsaken all his gold, and silver, and his precious things, which were in the land of Ammonihah, for the word of God, he being rejected by those who were once his friends and also by his father and his kindred;

documents.text: But they took their armies and went over into the borders of the land of Zarahemla, and fell upon the people who were in the land of Ammonihah and destroyed them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 25:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records Lamanite retaliation after slaying their brethren, including attacks on Ammonihah and battles with the Nephites. It reports the destruction of much of Amulon’s seed, their persecution of believing Lamanites by fire, and Lamanites then hunting Amulon’s remnant, fulfilling Abinadi’s words. Many Lamanites join Anti-Nephi-Lehi, bury weapons, keep commandments and the law of Moses while looking to Christ. Ammon and Aaron’s group rejoices.

documents.text: And many such things, yea, all manner of such things did they say unto them; and thus they did mock them for many days. And they did withhold food from them that they might hunger, and water that they might thirst; and they also did take from them their clothes that they were naked; and thus they were bound with strong cords, and confined in prison.

documents.text: And now behold, I have somewhat to say concerning the people of Ammon, who, in the beginning, were Lamanites; but by Ammon and his brethren, or rather by the power and word of God, they had been converted unto the Lord; and they had been brought down into the land of Zarahemla, and had ever since been protected by the Nephites.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 53:10** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records Moroni and Lehi securing Mulek, guarding Lamanite prisoners, and using them to bury the dead and fortify Bountiful with ditches and earthworks. It notes Nephite dissensions that allow Lamanites to take western cities. It recounts the people of Ammon’s oath against bloodshed, Helaman preventing them from breaking it, and 2,000 of their sons covenanting to fight under Helaman, who marches to the southwest borders.

documents.text: Now when the servants of the king saw an army pursuing after them, they were frightened again, and fled into the wilderness, and came over into the land of Zarahemla and joined the people of Ammon.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 47:29** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 36 verses and records Amalickiah stirring the Lamanites to war and receiving command to compel dissenters. He schemes at Onidah and mount Antipas, negotiates with Lehonti, and has Lehonti poisoned to become chief commander. Amalickiah returns to the city of Nephi, arranges the king’s assassination, and frames the king’s servants, who flee to Zarahemla and join the people of Ammon. He takes the city, convinces the queen, marries her, and is acknowledged king over Lamanites and Nephite dissenters.

documents.text: And it came to pass that he began to cry unto the people, saying: Behold, I am guilty, and these men are spotless before God. And he began to plead for them from that time forth; but they reviled him, saying: Art thou also possessed with the devil? And they spit upon him, and cast him out from among them, and also all those who believed in the words which had been spoken by Alma and Amulek; and they cast them out, and sent men to cast stones at them.

documents.text: Behold, now it came to pass that after the people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon, yea, and also after the Lamanites were driven out of the land, and their dead were buried by the people of the land—
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 30:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 60 verses and records peace in the 16th–17th years of the judges, Nephite observance of the law of Moses, and the rise of Korihor in Zarahemla preaching against prophecy, Christ, and accountability. Korihor is expelled from Jershon, taken in Gideon, and brought to Alma. After disputation and demanding a sign, Korihor is struck dumb, confesses deception, is cast out begging, and is killed among the Zoramites.

documents.text: Now they had sworn in their hearts that they would return to the land of Nephi, and if their wives and their children were slain, and also those that had tarried with them, that they would seek revenge, and also perish with them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 19:19** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 29 verses and records division among King Noah’s people, Gideon’s attempt to kill Noah, and the approach of a Lamanite army near Shemlon. The people flee; many are killed, and those remaining are spared and taken captive. The Lamanites allow them to possess the land under tribute and surrender of Noah. Noah is burned to death; priests flee. Limhi becomes king, swears tribute, and peace follows for two years under Lamanite guards.

query: How many days was Jesus in the tomb?

documents.text: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Genesis 50:3** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Joseph mourning Jacob, having Israel embalmed, and receiving Pharaoh’s permission to bury him in Canaan at Machpelah; a large Egyptian company accompanies the funeral and mourns at Atad. Joseph’s brothers fear revenge and seek forgiveness; Joseph reassures and provides for them. The chapter notes Joseph’s 110-year life, descendants through Ephraim and Manasseh, his prophecy of Israel’s return, his oath about his bones, and his death and embalming in Egypt.

documents.text: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 12:40** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 50 verses and records Jesus defending his disciples’ Sabbath grain picking, healing a man’s withered hand in a synagogue, and Pharisees plotting against him. Jesus heals many and commands silence, with an Isaiah citation. He casts out a demon from a blind, mute man, answers Beelzebub accusations, warns about blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, teaches about words and fruit, refuses a sign except Jonah, describes returning unclean spirits, and identifies doers of God’s will as family.

documents.text: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 11:9** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture.

documents.text: Therefore, there shall be one day and a night and a day, as if it were one day and there were no night; and this shall be unto you for a sign; for ye shall know of the rising of the sun and also of its setting; therefore they shall know of a surety that there shall be two days and a night; nevertheless the night shall not be darkened; and it shall be the night before he is born.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 14:4** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite prophesying signs of the Son of God’s birth in five years, including a night without darkness and a new star, and calling the people to repent. He also prophesies signs of Christ’s death: three days of darkness, thunderings, earthquakes, broken rocks, tempests, desolated cities, and opened graves with saints appearing. He teaches resurrection, repentance versus condemnation, and human agency to choose good or evil.

documents.text: After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Hosea 6:2** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 11 verses and records a call to return to the LORD for healing and revival, with promises of being raised up and knowing the LORD. It rebukes Ephraim and Judah for fleeting goodness and covenant transgression. The LORD states he desires mercy and knowledge of God over sacrifices. It condemns Gilead’s bloodshed, priests’ robbery and murder, Ephraim’s whoredom, Israel’s defilement, and announces a harvest judgment for Judah.

documents.text: And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Revelation 11:11** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records John measuring God’s temple while the outer court is left to Gentiles for 42 months. It covers two witnesses prophesying 1,260 days with power to judge and protect themselves, their death by the beast, public exposure, resurrection, and ascension, followed by an earthquake killing 7,000. The seventh trumpet sounds; heavenly voices, elders’ worship, judgment and rewards are announced, and God’s heavenly temple opens with the ark and signs.

documents.text: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 20:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Mary Magdalene finding the stone removed and reporting to Peter and the other disciple, who inspect the empty tomb and linen cloths. Mary sees two angels and then Jesus, who tells her to report to the disciples. Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his wounds, commissions them, gives the Holy Ghost, and speaks of remitting or retaining sins. Thomas doubts, then sees Jesus and confesses him. The chapter states the purpose of the written signs.

documents.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 11:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture.

documents.text: But behold, as I said unto you concerning another sign, a sign of his death, behold, in that day that he shall suffer death the sun shall be darkened and refuse to give his light unto you; and also the moon and the stars; and there shall be no light upon the face of this land, even from the time that he shall suffer death, for the space of three days, to the time that he shall rise again from the dead.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 14:20** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite prophesying signs of the Son of God’s birth in five years, including a night without darkness and a new star, and calling the people to repent. He teaches resurrection, repentance versus condemnation, and human agency to choose good or evil.

documents.text: Being forty days tempted of the devil. And in those days he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungered.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 4:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 44 verses and records Jesus’ forty-day temptation in the wilderness and his Scripture responses. It covers his return to Galilee, teaching in synagogues, and reading Isaiah in Nazareth, declaring its fulfillment, and being rejected and threatened. It describes ministry in Capernaum: casting out an unclean spirit, healing Simon’s mother-in-law and many sick, silencing demons, withdrawing to a desert place, and continuing to preach in Galilee.

documents.text: Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 12:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 50 verses and records Jesus in Bethany where Mary anoints his feet and Judas objects; chief priests plan to kill Lazarus. It covers Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem with palm branches, Greeks seeking him, and teachings on his coming death, serving him, and being the light. A heavenly voice speaks; Jesus explains judgment and belief, notes unbelief fulfilling Isaiah, and affirms speaking the Father’s commandment.

documents.text: Therefore, I would that ye should behold that the Lord truly did teach the people, for the space of three days; and after that he did show himself unto them oft, and did break bread oft, and bless it, and give it unto them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 26:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Jesus expounding all things to the multitude, including future events through the final judgment and resurrection. Mormon states only a small part of Jesus’s teachings is written; greater things are withheld or revealed based on faith, and the Lord forbids recording some sayings. Jesus teaches three days, appears often, breaks bread, heals, raises a man, and ascends. Children speak forbidden words. Disciples baptize; converts receive the Holy Ghost, live justly with all things common, and are called the church of Christ.

documents.text: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 27:63** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 66 verses and records the chief priests and elders delivering Jesus to Pilate; Judas returning thirty pieces of silver, hanging himself, and the purchase of the potter’s field. Pilate offers Barabbas, washes his hands, and hands Jesus over for scourging and crucifixion. Soldiers mock Jesus; Simon of Cyrene carries the cross; Jesus is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves amid darkness and temple signs. Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus, and the tomb is sealed and guarded.

documents.text: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 1:3** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Jesus’ post-resurrection appearances and teaching for forty days, his command to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, and his ascension from the Mount of Olives. Two men in white speak of his return. The apostles and others pray together in Jerusalem. Peter addresses about 120 disciples about Judas’ death and the “field of blood,” cites Psalms, and Matthias is chosen by lot to replace Judas.

documents.text: And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 9:9** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Saul obtaining letters to arrest disciples in Damascus, encountering a heavenly light and Jesus, becoming blind, and being healed and baptized through Ananias. Saul preaches in Damascus, escapes a plot, and is accepted in Jerusalem through Barnabas before being sent to Tarsus. It also covers church growth, Peter healing Aeneas in Lydda, raising Tabitha in Joppa, and staying with Simon the tanner.

documents.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 11:39** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture.

documents.text: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 14:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 72 verses and records priests and scribes plotting to kill Jesus, a woman anointing him in Bethany, and Judas arranging betrayal. Jesus directs Passover preparations, predicts a betrayer, and institutes bread and cup at the meal. He foretells disciples’ scattering and Peter’s denial, prays in Gethsemane, and is arrested. Jesus is tried before the high priest and council, condemned, mocked, and beaten. Peter denies Jesus three times before the cock crows twice and weeps.

documents.text: Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 26:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 75 verses and records chief priests and elders under Caiaphas plotting to kill Jesus; a woman anoints Jesus in Bethany; Judas agrees to betray him for thirty pieces of silver. Jesus prepares and eats the Passover, predicts betrayal, institutes bread and cup, and foretells Peter’s denial. In Gethsemane Jesus prays and urges watchfulness; Judas leads an armed crowd to arrest him. Jesus is taken to Caiaphas, questioned with false witnesses, condemned, mocked, and Peter denies Jesus three times.

documents.text: And it came to pass that after two days and two nights they were about to take his body and lay it in a sepulchre, which they had made for the purpose of burying their dead.

query: Who translated the Book of Mormon?

documents.text: Two days after the arrival of Mr. Cowdery (being the 7th of April) I commenced to translate the Book of Mormon, and he began to write for me.

It covers Moroni’s 1823 visits about gold plates, Urim and Thummim, annual meetings, and warnings. It records obtaining and safeguarding the plates (1827), moving to Pennsylvania, early translation, Martin Harris’s Anthon visit, Oliver Cowdery as scribe, and John the Baptist conferring Aaronic Priesthood and commanding baptism (May 1829).

It recounts calling Joseph Smith and others to establish the church, translate the Book of Mormon, and proclaim the gospel, with promises of forgiveness for repentance and fulfillment of the Lord’s word.

It covers basic doctrines of creation, fall, atonement, repentance, baptism, and endurance. It gives requirements and wording for baptism and the sacrament prayers, outlines duties and authority of elders, priests, teachers, and deacons, sets conference and ordination procedures, and provides rules for membership records, discipline, children’s blessings, and letters of standing.

I have actually seen a vision; and who am I that I can withstand God, or why does the world think to make me deny what I have actually seen? This chapter contains 25 verses and covers exhortations to continue brotherly love, show hospitality, remember prisoners, honor marriage, avoid covetousness, and trust God’s help. It urges respect for spiritual leaders and avoidance of strange doctrines. It references Jesus suffering outside the gate, seeking a future city, offering praise and doing good. The writer requests prayer, mentions Timothy’s release, sends greetings, and gives a benediction.

documents.text: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:6** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling.

documents.text: That thou mayest love the LORD thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 30:20** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Moses promising Israel’s restoration if they repent and obey: God gathers them from exile, returns them to their land, prospers them, and “circumcises” their heart; curses fall on enemies. It states the commandment is accessible and near. Moses sets before them life and death, blessing and curse, urges choosing life by loving and obeying the LORD, warning against idolatry and perishing.

documents.text: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Colossians 3:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records exhortations to seek things above with Christ, put to death sinful practices, and put off anger, malice, and lying while putting on the new person. It lists virtues such as mercy, kindness, humility, patience, forgiveness, love, peace, thankfulness, and worshipful teaching. It gives household commands for wives, husbands, children, fathers, and servants, urging wholehearted service to the Lord and impartial judgment for wrongdoing.

documents.text: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
documents.context: The following passage is from **Romans 6:16** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records Paul teaching that believers, baptized into Jesus Christ’s death, are to walk in newness of life and consider themselves dead to sin and alive to God. He commands not letting sin reign, not yielding members to unrighteousness, but yielding to God as instruments of righteousness. He contrasts servitude to sin leading to death with obedience leading to holiness and eternal life, concluding with wages of sin versus God’s gift through Christ.

documents.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ephesians 6:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 24 verses and covers instructions for children to obey parents and for fathers to nurture without provoking; servants to obey masters sincerely and masters to forbear threatening. It urges believers to be strong, put on the whole armor of God against spiritual powers, and pray continually. Paul requests prayer for bold gospel speech as an imprisoned ambassador, sends Tychicus with news, and closes with peace and grace.

documents.text: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Colossians 3:20** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records exhortations to seek things above with Christ, put to death sinful practices, and put off anger, malice, and lying while putting on the new person. It lists virtues such as mercy, kindness, humility, patience, forgiveness, love, peace, thankfulness, and worshipful teaching. It gives household commands for wives, husbands, children, fathers, and servants, urging wholehearted service to the Lord and impartial judgment for wrongdoing.

documents.text: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 7:23** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records the LORD’s message to Jeremiah to preach at the temple gate in Jerusalem, calling Judah to amend conduct, execute justice, and stop oppression, bloodshed, theft, adultery, false oaths, and idolatry. It warns that trusting in the temple will not prevent judgment, citing Shiloh. Jeremiah is told not to intercede. It condemns worship of the “queen of heaven,” temple defilement, and child sacrifice at Tophet in the valley of Hinnom, forecasting slaughter, exile, and desolation.

documents.text: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Romans 16:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Paul commending Phebe of the church at Cenchrea and instructing the Romans to receive and assist her. He sends greetings to many believers and households in Rome, including Priscilla and Aquila and their house church, and relays greetings from his companions. He commands mutual greeting, warns against divisive deceivers, promises God will bruise Satan, and closes with a doxology about the revealed gospel.

documents.text: And the people said unto Joshua, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joshua 24:24** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records Joshua gathering Israel at Shechem, recounting God’s acts from Terah and Abraham through the exodus, wilderness, and conquest. Joshua commands the people to fear and serve the LORD, put away foreign gods, and choose whom to serve. Israel pledges obedience; Joshua makes a covenant, writes it, and sets a stone witness. It records Joshua’s death and burial, Israel’s continued service, Joseph’s bones buried at Shechem, and Eleazar’s death.

documents.text: Ye shall walk after the LORD your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 13:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records laws against apostasy and idolatry. It commands Israel not to heed prophets or dreamers whose signs lead to other gods, but to fear and obey the LORD. It requires execution of close relatives or friends who entice to idolatry. It orders investigation of an apostate city and, if confirmed, its destruction, burning of spoil, and prohibition of rebuilding.

documents.text: But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Exodus 23:22** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records laws on truthful testimony, impartial justice, aiding an enemy’s livestock, rejecting bribery, and not oppressing strangers. It commands sabbath rest, a sabbatical year for fields, and forbids naming other gods. It institutes three annual feasts and offerings. God promises an Angel to lead Israel, defeat Canaanite nations, set borders, and forbids covenants or idol worship.

documents.text: Observe and hear all these words which I command thee, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee for ever, when thou doest that which is good and right in the sight of the LORD thy God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 12:28** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records commands to destroy Canaanite worship sites and images, and to worship only at the place the LORD chooses. It requires bringing sacrifices, tithes, vows, and offerings there, rejoicing with households and Levites, and not offering burnt offerings elsewhere. It permits eating meat in towns but forbids eating blood. It warns against adopting pagan practices and commands not to add to or diminish the statutes.

documents.text: Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 5:29** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 42 verses and records Ananias and Sapphira selling land, withholding part of the price, being confronted by Peter for lying, and dying, causing fear in the church. It covers apostles doing signs and healings in Jerusalem, including Peter’s shadow. The Sadducees imprison the apostles; an angel frees them to teach in the temple. They appear before the council; Peter testifies of Jesus. Gamaliel advises restraint; the apostles are beaten, warned, and continue preaching daily.

documents.text: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Exodus 19:5** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Israel arriving in the wilderness of Sinai and camping before Mount Sinai. The LORD calls Moses up, recounts deliverance from Egypt, and offers a covenant requiring obedience; the people agree. The LORD commands sanctification, washing, and boundaries around the mountain with death penalties for violation. On the third day thunder, lightning, trumpet, smoke, and quaking accompany the LORD’s descent; Moses speaks with God, is warned to restrain the people, and is told to return with Aaron.

documents.text: If ye will fear the LORD, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the LORD your God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 12:14** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Samuel’s address to Israel after appointing a king. Samuel asks the people to testify that he has not defrauded or oppressed them, and they affirm it. He recounts the LORD’s deliverances from Egypt and through judges, notes Israel’s request for a king when Nahash threatens, and warns obedience brings favor while rebellion brings judgment. Samuel calls thunder and rain at wheat harvest; the people fear and ask prayer. Samuel urges wholehearted service and warns both people and king face destruction if they persist in wickedness.

documents.text: But if ye will not obey the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall the hand of the LORD be against you, as it was against your fathers.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 12:15** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Samuel’s address to Israel after appointing a king. Samuel asks the people to testify that he has not defrauded or oppressed them, and they affirm it. He recounts the LORD’s deliverances from Egypt and through judges, notes Israel’s request for a king when Nahash threatens, and warns obedience brings favor while rebellion brings judgment. Samuel calls thunder and rain at wheat harvest; the people fear and ask prayer. Samuel urges wholehearted service and warns both people and king face destruction if they persist in wickedness.

documents.text: Again I say unto you, hearken and hear and obey the law which I shall give unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 42:2** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 93 verses and records instructions to assembled elders to preach and baptize, travel west, and await revelation on New Jerusalem; affirms Edward Partridge’s office and requires authorized ordination. It gives commandments (no murder, theft, lying, adultery; marital fidelity; avoid evil speaking, pride, idleness), establishes consecration, stewardships, storehouse, and support for poor and leaders, outlines care and healing of the sick, and details church discipline and trials with witnesses and referral to civil law.

documents.text: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 15:24** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Samuel commanding Saul to destroy Amalek completely. Saul musters Israel at Telaim, warns the Kenites to depart, defeats Amalek from Havilah to Shur, but spares King Agag and the best livestock. God tells Samuel he rejects Saul for disobedience. Samuel confronts Saul at Gilgal, declares obedience above sacrifice, and announces the kingdom is torn from Saul. Samuel executes Agag, returns to Ramah, and no longer visits Saul.

query: What is the plan of salvation?

documents.text: And now, behold, I say unto you: This is the plan of salvation unto all men, through the blood of mine Only Begotten, who shall come in the meridian of time.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:62** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: Therefore God gave unto them commandments, after having made known unto them the plan of redemption, that they should not do evil, the penalty thereof being a second death, which was an everlasting death as to things pertaining unto righteousness; for on such the plan of redemption could have no power, for the works of justice could not be destroyed, according to the supreme goodness of God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:32** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. He teaches resurrection and judgment by works, including a second spiritual death for the unrepentant. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: O how great the plan of our God! For on the other hand, the paradise of God must deliver up the spirits of the righteous, and the grave deliver up the body of the righteous; and the spirit and the body is restored to itself again, and all men become incorruptible, and immortal, and they are living souls, having a perfect knowledge like unto us in the flesh, save it be that our knowledge shall be perfect.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 9:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jacob teaching about the Lord’s covenants with Israel, the fall, death, resurrection, and an infinite atonement. He describes judgment, paradise, hell, and restoration of body and spirit. He commands repentance, faith, baptism, and enduring to the end, explains accountability under law, pronounces woes on specific sins, and urges humility, prayer, and coming to the Holy One of Israel.

documents.text: Yea, I would that ye would come forth and harden not your hearts any longer; for behold, now is the time and the day of your salvation; and therefore, if ye will repent and harden not your hearts, immediately shall the great plan of redemption be brought about unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:31** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: Now, if it had not been for the plan of redemption, which was laid from the foundation of the world, there could have been no resurrection of the dead; but there was a plan of redemption laid, which shall bring to pass the resurrection of the dead, of which has been spoken.

Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: And now behold, if it were possible that our first parents could have gone forth and partaken of the tree of life they would have been forever miserable, having no preparatory state; and thus the plan of redemption would have been frustrated, and the word of God would have been void, taking none effect.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:26** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: And now, the plan of mercy could not be brought about except an atonement should be made; therefore God himself atoneth for the sins of the world, to bring about the plan of mercy, to appease the demands of justice, that God might be a perfect, just God, and a merciful God also.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 42:15** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching.

documents.text: Now I say unto you that ye must repent, and be born again; for the Spirit saith if ye are not born again ye cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven; therefore come and be baptized unto repentance, that ye may be washed from your sins, that ye may have faith on the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world, who is mighty to save and to cleanse from all unrighteousness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 7:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Alma speaking at Gideon after leaving the judgment-seat, expressing hope the people are faithful, and urging repentance and preparation for the Son of God. He prophesies Christ’s birth to Mary at Jerusalem and describes his suffering, death, and taking sins and infirmities. Alma commands being born again, baptism, covenant keeping, humility, patience, prayer, gratitude, and having faith, hope, and charity, then pronounces blessings and peace.

documents.text: And they began from that time forth to call on his name; therefore God conversed with men, and made known unto them the plan of redemption, which had been prepared from the foundation of the world; and this he made known unto them according to their faith and repentance and their holy works.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:30** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: And thus mercy can satisfy the demands of justice, and encircles them in the arms of safety, while he that exercises no faith unto repentance is exposed to the whole law of the demands of justice; therefore only unto him that has faith unto repentance is brought about the great and eternal plan of redemption.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:16** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: I say unto thee, my son, that the plan of restoration is requisite with the justice of God; for it is requisite that all things should be restored to their proper order. Behold, it is requisite and just, according to the power and resurrection of Christ, that the soul of man should be restored to its body, and that every part of the body should be restored to itself.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 41:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 15 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the doctrine of restoration: resurrection restores soul to body and all things to proper order. People are judged by works and heart’s desires, receiving good for good or evil for evil, happiness or misery. God’s decrees are unalterable; individuals choose. Alma warns restoration does not return sin to happiness, defines restoration as like for like, and commands mercy, justice, righteous judgment, and continual good.

documents.text: For behold, if Adam had put forth his hand immediately, and partaken of the tree of life, he would have lived forever, according to the word of God, having no space for repentance; yea, and also the word of God would have been void, and the great plan of salvation would have been frustrated.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 42:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching.

documents.text: I say, that this is the man who receiveth salvation, through the atonement which was prepared from the foundation of the world for all mankind, which ever were since the fall of Adam, or who are, or who ever shall be, even unto the end of the world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 4:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records King Benjamin’s people falling down, pleading for mercy through Christ’s atoning blood, and receiving joy and remission of sins. Benjamin commands belief in God, repentance, humility, prayer, and steadfast faith. He instructs them to live peaceably, teach children, and succor the poor by sharing substance, feeding, clothing, and visiting the sick, in wisdom and order, returning borrowed goods, watching thoughts, words, and deeds, and keeping commandments to avoid perishing.

documents.text: Therefore, whoso repenteth and cometh unto me as a little child, him will I receive, for of such is the kingdom of God. Behold, for such I have laid down my life, and have taken it up again; therefore repent, and come unto me ye ends of the earth, and be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 9:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records a voice speaking to all the land, pronouncing woe and urging repentance after widespread destructions. It names cities destroyed by fire, sinking, burial, or flooding, including Zarahemla, Moroni, Moronihah, Gilgal, Onihah, Mocum, Jerusalem, Gadiandi, Gadiomnah, Jacob, Gimgimno, Jacobugath, Laman, Josh, Gad, and Kishkumen. Jesus Christ identifies himself, offers mercy and eternal life, fulfills the law of Moses, ends blood sacrifices, and commands offering a broken heart and contrite spirit.

documents.text: Therefore, according to justice, the plan of redemption could not be brought about, only on conditions of repentance of men in this probationary state, yea, this preparatory state; for except it were for these conditions, mercy could not take effect except it should destroy the work of justice. Now the work of justice could not be destroyed; if so, God would cease to be God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 42:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching.

documents.text: Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do; for, for this cause have they been shown unto me, that ye might know the gate by which ye should enter. For the gate by which ye should enter is repentance and baptism by water; and then cometh a remission of your sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 31:17** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Nephi’s plain statement of the doctrine of Christ. He references the Lamb of God’s baptism, the descent of the Holy Ghost, and the strait and narrow path. He commands repentance, baptism in Christ’s name, receiving the Holy Ghost and baptism of fire, and warns against later denial. He teaches pressing forward, feasting on Christ’s words, and enduring to the end to gain eternal life.

documents.text: For as death hath passed upon all men, to fulfil the merciful plan of the great Creator, there must needs be a power of resurrection, and the resurrection must needs come unto man by reason of the fall; and the fall came by reason of transgression; and because man became fallen they were cut off from the presence of the Lord.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 9:6** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jacob teaching about the Lord’s covenants with Israel, the fall, death, resurrection, and an infinite atonement. He describes judgment, paradise, hell, and restoration of body and spirit. He commands repentance, faith, baptism, and enduring to the end, explains accountability under law, pronounces woes on specific sins, and urges humility, prayer, and coming to the Holy One of Israel.

documents.text: For no man can be saved, according to the words of Christ, save they shall have faith in his name; wherefore, if these things have ceased, then has faith ceased also; and awful is the state of man, for they are as though there had been no redemption made.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 7:38** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 48 verses and records Moroni quoting Mormon’s synagogue discourse on faith, hope, and charity. Mormon teaches judging good and evil by the light of Christ and that actions require real intent. He explains faith in Christ brings good gifts, miracles, angelic ministry, and repentance, and commands baptism. He defines hope through Christ’s atonement and resurrection and gives charity’s attributes, urging prayer to be filled with Christlike love.

documents.text: That by reason of transgression cometh the fall, which fall bringeth death, and inasmuch as ye were born into the world by water, and blood, and the spirit, which I have made, and so became of dust a living soul, even so ye must be born again into the kingdom of heaven, of water, and of the Spirit, and be cleansed by blood, even the blood of mine Only Begotten; that ye might be sanctified from all sin, and enjoy the words of eternal life in this world, and eternal life in the world to come, even immortal glory;

query: How do the Bible and Book of Mormon both describe the Messiah?

documents.text: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground; he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him there is no beauty that we should desire him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 14:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 12 verses and records Isaiah’s prophecy of the Lord’s servant: he grows up without comeliness, is despised and rejected, bears griefs and sorrows, is wounded for others’ transgressions, and is likened to a lamb led to slaughter without protest. It describes his unjust cutting off, burial with the wicked and rich, being an offering for sin, justifying many, and being rewarded after bearing sins and interceding for transgressors.

documents.text: And lo, he shall suffer temptations, and pain of body, hunger, thirst, and fatigue, even more than man can suffer, except it be unto death; for behold, blood cometh from every pore, so great shall be his anguish for the wickedness and the abominations of his people.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 3:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records King Benjamin relating an angel’s message about Jesus Christ’s coming: His mortal birth to Mary, miracles, suffering, crucifixion, resurrection, and judgment. It covers the atonement for Adam’s transgression and ignorant sin, and requires repentance and faith for willful rebellion. It notes the law of Moses as types of Christ, declares little children blameless, describes yielding to the Holy Spirit, and warns of judgment and punishment for evil works.

documents.text: And the Lord said: Blessed is he through whose seed Messiah shall come; for he saith—I am Messiah, the King of Zion, the Rock of Heaven, which is broad as eternity; whoso cometh in at the gate and climbeth up by me shall never fall; wherefore, blessed are they of whom I have spoken, for they shall come forth with songs of everlasting joy.

This chapter contains 58 verses and records Paul’s summary of the gospel: Christ dies, is buried, rises, and appears to Cephas, the Twelve, many brethren, James, the apostles, and Paul. It argues that denying resurrection makes faith and preaching vain, then outlines resurrection order and Christ’s reign until death is destroyed. It mentions baptism for the dead, warns against corrupting associations, explains resurrection bodies, and commands steadfast labor.

documents.text: And this death of which I have spoken, which is the spiritual death, shall deliver up its dead; which spiritual death is hell; wherefore, death and hell must deliver up their dead, and hell must deliver up its captive spirits, and the grave must deliver up its captive bodies, and the bodies and the spirits of men will be restored one to the other; and it is by the power of the resurrection of the Holy One of Israel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 9:12** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jacob teaching about the Lord’s covenants with Israel, the fall, death, resurrection, and an infinite atonement. He describes judgment, paradise, hell, and restoration of body and spirit. He commands repentance, faith, baptism, and enduring to the end, explains accountability under law, pronounces woes on specific sins, and urges humility, prayer, and coming to the Holy One of Israel.

documents.text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

Christ does not visit the wicked but commissions righteous messengers to preach repentance, faith, and vicarious ordinances to spirits in darkness. Adam, Eve, Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, prophets, Nephite prophets, and latter-day leaders are present; temple work and continued missionary labor among the dead are described.

documents.text: And because of the redemption of man, which came by Jesus Christ, they are brought back into the presence of the Lord; yea, this is wherein all men are redeemed, because the death of Christ bringeth to pass the resurrection, which bringeth to pass a redemption from an endless sleep, from which sleep all men shall be awakened by the power of God when the trump shall sound; and they shall come forth, both small and great, and all shall stand before his bar, being redeemed and loosed from this eternal band of death, which death is a temporal death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 9:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Moroni warning unbelievers about Christ’s coming, judgment, and guilt before God, urging repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. It addresses denial of revelation and miracles, affirming God’s unchanging nature, creation, the Fall, redemption, resurrection, and final judgment. It cites signs following believers and commands preaching, baptism, and worthy sacrament. Moroni explains record imperfections, reformed Egyptian language, interpretation means, and prays for Israel’s covenant and restoration.

documents.text: And ye shall never endure the pains of death; but when I shall come in my glory ye shall be changed in the twinkling of an eye from mortality to immortality; and then shall ye be blessed in the kingdom of my Father.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 28:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records Jesus asking the Nephite disciples what they desire after his departure. Nine request to end their ministry and come to him at age seventy-two; three desire to remain and bring souls to Christ and are promised they will not taste death. They are transfigured, forbidden to reveal what they see, and continue ministering, baptizing, and giving the Holy Ghost. They escape prisons, pits, furnaces, and beasts unharmed; Mormon notes their future ministry among Gentiles, Jews, and Israel and explains their bodily change until judgment.

documents.text: But there is a resurrection, therefore the grave hath no victory, and the sting of death is swallowed up in Christ.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 16:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 15 verses and records Abinadi’s teachings that all peoples will witness the Lord’s salvation and confess God’s just judgments, while the wicked are cast out for refusing to hearken. It covers the Fall, humanity’s lost state, and redemption through Christ’s coming and resurrection. It describes universal resurrection and final judgment by works, with contrasting outcomes, calls to repent, and instructs that the law of Moses is a shadow pointing to redemption through Christ.

documents.text: For all the rest shall be brought forth by the resurrection of the dead, through the triumph and the glory of the Lamb, who was slain, who was in the bosom of the Father before the worlds were made.

This chapter contains 119 verses and records a February 16, 1832 vision given to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon while translating John 5. They testify of Jesus Christ at the Father’s right hand, Lucifer’s fall, and the fate of sons of perdition. It outlines resurrection and final judgment and describes celestial, terrestrial, and telestial glories, including the church of the Firstborn, spirits in prison, and varying inheritances and ministries.

He teaches resurrection, a first resurrection for prophets, the obedient, the ignorant, and little children, and excludes willful rebels. He foresees salvation proclaimed to all nations and Zion/Jerusalem restored.

documents.text: The soul shall be restored to the body, and the body to the soul; yea, and every limb and joint shall be restored to its body; yea, even a hair of the head shall not be lost; but all things shall be restored to their proper and perfect frame.

Spirits return to God; the righteous enter paradise and rest, and the wicked enter darkness and misery. Alma distinguishes spirit states from bodily resurrection, describes restoration of body and soul, and judgment according to works.

query: What do scriptures say about caring for the poor?

documents.text: And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 4:26** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records King Benjamin’s people falling down, pleading for mercy through Christ’s atoning blood, and receiving joy and remission of sins. Benjamin commands belief in God, repentance, humility, prayer, and steadfast faith. He instructs them to live peaceably, teach children, and succor the poor by sharing substance, feeding, clothing, and visiting the sick, in wisdom and order, returning borrowed goods, watching thoughts, words, and deeds, and keeping commandments to avoid perishing.

documents.text: And after ye have obtained a hope in Christ ye shall obtain riches, if ye seek them; and ye will seek them for the intent to do good—to clothe the naked, and to feed the hungry, and to liberate the captive, and administer relief to the sick and the afflicted.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jacob 2:19** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jacob speaking in the temple after Nephi’s death, declaring God’s word to the Nephites. He condemns pride, costly apparel, and persecution tied to riches, commanding them to seek God first and use wealth to help others. He then condemns whoredoms and plural wives, cites David and Solomon, commands one wife and no concubines, warns of curses, and notes the sorrow of wives and children.

documents.text: Wo unto you rich men, that will not give your substance to the poor, for your riches will canker your souls; and this shall be your lamentation in the day of visitation, and of judgment, and of indignation: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and my soul is not saved!
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 56:16** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records the Lord warning the rebellious and requiring disciples to take up the cross and keep commandments. It revokes and reassigns missions: Thomas B. Marsh travels to Missouri with Selah J. Griffin; Newel Knight remains with Saints in Thompson and leads contrite members who go. Ezra Thayre is commanded to repent, resolve land issues, or be cut off. The Lord rebukes sins, warns rich and unrighteous poor, and promises recompense, deliverance, and inheritance to the contrite poor.

documents.text: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 14:7** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 72 verses and records priests and scribes plotting to kill Jesus, a woman anointing him in Bethany, and Judas arranging betrayal. Jesus directs Passover preparations, predicts a betrayer, and institutes bread and cup at the meal. He foretells disciples’ scattering and Peter’s denial, prays in Gethsemane, and is arrested. Jesus is tried before the high priest and council, condemned, mocked, and beaten. Peter denies Jesus three times before the cock crows twice and weeps.

documents.text: Behold, I say unto you, that ye must visit the poor and the needy and administer to their relief, that they may be kept until all things may be done according to my law which ye have received. Amen.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 44:6** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord directing that the church elders be called together from all directions by letter or other means. He promises to pour out His Spirit on the faithful at their assembly. The elders are to preach repentance in surrounding regions, leading to conversions and power to organize under civil law for protection and preservation. They are commanded to visit and relieve the poor and needy.

documents.text: Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Amos 5:11** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records a lamentation over Israel’s fall and coming depletion. It commands Israel to seek the LORD to live and not to seek Beth-el, Gilgal, or Beer-sheba. It condemns injustice, oppression of the poor, bribery, and rejecting upright rebuke. It announces widespread wailing and that the day of the LORD is darkness. It rejects feasts, sacrifices, and songs without justice, recalls wilderness idolatry (Moloch, Chiun), and foretells captivity beyond Damascus.

documents.text: And now behold, my beloved brethren, I say unto you, do not suppose that this is all; for after ye have done all these things, if ye turn away the needy, and the naked, and visit not the sick and afflicted, and impart of your substance, if ye have, to those who stand in need—I say unto you, if ye do not any of these things, behold, your prayer is vain, and availeth you nothing, and ye are as hypocrites who do deny the faith.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:28** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 15:11** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records laws for a seven-year debt release among Israelites, allowing collection from foreigners. It commands generosity to the poor and forbids withholding loans because the release year approaches. It mandates freeing Hebrew servants in the seventh year with liberal provisions, with an ear-piercing rite for lifelong service. It also requires dedicating firstborn male herd and flock, eating them at the chosen place, rejecting blemished animals, and forbidding blood consumption.

documents.text: Verily, verily, I say that I would that ye should do alms unto the poor; but take heed that ye do not your alms before men to be seen of them; otherwise ye have no reward of your Father who is in heaven.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 13:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus’ instructions on giving alms, praying, and fasting in secret rather than for public praise. It gives a model prayer and commands forgiveness of others. It warns against storing earthly treasures, serving God and Mammon, and having an evil eye. Jesus charges the twelve to minister and teaches not to worry about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Proverbs 22:9** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 29 verses and covers proverbs on valuing a good name over riches, God as maker of rich and poor, prudence, humility, avoiding froward ways, child training and discipline, debt and oppression, generosity to the poor, removing scoffers, purity of speech, laziness, adultery temptation, heeding wise counsel, protecting the poor in court, avoiding angry companions, not guaranteeing debts, keeping ancient landmarks, and diligence rewarded before kings.

documents.text: For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Psalms 72:12** from the **Old Testament**. It describes lasting fear of the LORD, peace, and flourishing righteousness. It covers the king’s dominion from sea to sea, nations and kings bringing gifts (Tarshish, Sheba, Seba), and universal service. It ends with praise to the LORD and a note that David’s prayers are ended.

documents.text: And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners of thy field when thou reapest, neither shalt thou gather any gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor, and to the stranger: I am the LORD your God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Leviticus 23:22** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 44 verses and records the LORD’s instructions to Moses for Israel’s appointed feasts and holy convocations: the weekly Sabbath, Passover, and the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread; firstfruits and the wave sheaf with required offerings; counting fifty days to the feast of weeks with wave loaves and sacrifices; gleaning for poor and stranger; memorial of trumpets; Day of Atonement with fasting and work prohibitions; and the seven-day Feast of Tabernacles with an eighth-day assembly, booths, and specified branches.

documents.text: Thy congregation hath dwelt therein: thou, O God, hast prepared of thy goodness for the poor.

It mentions ascending and receiving gifts, deliverance from death, defeat of enemies, sanctuary procession, tribes, Jerusalem temple tribute, and nations praising God.

This chapter contains 42 verses and records the Lord identifying Himself as Jesus Christ, warning of corruption, hidden plots, and coming judgment, and calling the Saints to prepare and be purified. documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 8:37** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Moroni finishing Mormon’s record after Cumorah, reporting the Nephites’ destruction, Mormon’s death, and Moroni alone hiding the plates. He notes ongoing Lamanite violence and ministry from surviving disciples of Jesus. Moroni explains the record’s purpose and limits, warns against condemning it, urges searching Isaiah, and prophesies the record coming forth amid denied miracles, wars, disasters, secret combinations, corrupt churches, pride, and neglect of the poor.

documents.text: And behold, thou wilt remember the poor, and consecrate of thy properties for their support that which thou hast to impart unto them, with a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 42:30** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 93 verses and records instructions to assembled elders to preach and baptize, travel west, and await revelation on New Jerusalem; affirms Edward Partridge’s office and requires authorized ordination. It gives commandments (no murder, theft, lying, adultery; marital fidelity; avoid evil speaking, pride, idleness), establishes consecration, stewardships, storehouse, and support for poor and leaders, outlines care and healing of the sick, and details church discipline and trials with witnesses and referral to civil law.

documents.text: He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.

It separates Kirtland and Zion orders, establishes sacred and general treasuries, regulates common-consent withdrawals, and commands paying debts, seeking loans, and writing to New York.

query: How is the fall of Adam described in different scriptures?

documents.text: Now Alma said unto him: This is the thing which I was about to explain. Now we see that Adam did fall by the partaking of the forbidden fruit, according to the word of God; and thus we see, that by his fall, all mankind became a lost and fallen people.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. He teaches resurrection and judgment by works, including a second spiritual death for the unrepentant. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: But behold, it was appointed unto man to die—therefore, as they were cut off from the tree of life they should be cut off from the face of the earth—and man became lost forever, yea, they became fallen man.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 42:6** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching.

documents.text: And I, the Lord God, caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam; and he slept, and I took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in the stead thereof;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 3:21** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records God finishing creation, resting, blessing and sanctifying the seventh day, and stating that creations are made spiritually before naturally. God forms Adam, plants the Garden of Eden, places the tree of life and the tree of knowledge, and describes Eden’s river and its four branches. Adam is commanded not to eat the forbidden tree, names animals, and Eve is created from his rib; marriage is instituted.

documents.text: And the Gods caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam; and he slept, and they took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in the stead thereof;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Abraham 5:15** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. It describes mist watering the ground, the creation of man from dust with his spirit, and the planting of Eden with the tree of life and the tree of knowledge. It includes the command not to eat the forbidden tree, the creation of woman from Adam’s rib, marriage, nakedness without shame, and Adam naming animals.

documents.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 2:25** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Lehi’s counsel to Jacob about afflictions, redemption through the Holy Messiah, and resurrection. It covers law, sin, and atonement; opposition in all things; creation and the Fall of Adam and Eve; the devil’s role; probation and repentance. Lehi teaches human agency to choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death, and urges obedience to the Mediator’s commandments.

documents.text: And now behold, I say unto you that if it had been possible for Adam to have partaken of the fruit of the tree of life at that time, there would have been no death, and the word would have been void, making God a liar, for he said: If thou eat thou shalt surely die.
